- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate mean reversion window and reduce forecast volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in early days (e.g., day 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply a 0.5–1% upward bias to first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral or bearish), model tends to overcorrect; apply a 1–2% downward bias to avoid overbought signals.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — add a 0.5–1% upward bias to mid-horizon to capture rebound.
